selectionReason: The next fifteen, in source-row order, of the 271 absent frozen rows at least one of whose KANJIDIC2 readings is used by an existing word article that declares the kanji (an automatic alignment of each word's kana against the kanji's readings), the rule announced on issue 60 after batch 136. No word article is added: 20 existing articles each gain one link to a new card. A card quizzes each reading that a declaring word article uses, unless the pinned JMdict marks the spelling as ateji or the reading as gikun; name-only readings are never quizzed; a reading type with no such reading gets an empty quizzed list. All fifteen pass, so none is set aside. The 湧く article also drops its remark that neither 湧 nor 涌 has a card. Two cards also change in one remark: the 渋 card's remark that said 滞 had no card here now links 滞, and the 暑 card's remark that said there was no card for 炎 to exclude now links 炎 and says it mainly names fire. 136 rows of the 271 group, 11 rows whose declaring articles use none of their KANJIDIC2 readings, and 644 rows with no declaring article remain.

Some readings on the cards rest on a single dictionary entry or a Kanjipedia-only entry and are labelled as source-only where they appear; the card text is the authority for which.
Some titles share an English word with existing titles in another sense and are not excluded from each other's quiz options, except where a Notes bullet on the card says otherwise.
Each mnemonic is a modern-shape memory aid, labelled on the card as not etymology.
The reading audits are the author's Python ports of the Kotlin builder; no Kotlin cross-check was run.

The scope audits do not attribute reads made through shell commands or Python, so they list cards and other files as unread that the reports say were read; the second Claude confirmation covered only the two changed lines and the GPT confirmation the cumulative change, so neither re-read the unchanged cards or any word article beyond 湧く.
